cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's people scattered across five regions (1 Peter 1:1). He's already told them the old crowd heaps abuse on them for not joining in the wild life anymore (1 Peter 4:4). Now he calls them 'Beloved' and names what they're going through: a fiery trial.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to treat their fiery trial as something strange and unexpected.

cards.text: FIERY, friend? I bake next to ovens all day, and that's the word right before I smell my own mustache. But Peter's answer to the heat is NOT what you'd expect.

cards.question: Instead of being surprised by the fiery trial, Peter tells them to ___.
Peter tells these believers to rejoice in their fiery trial. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Their enemies will soon give up

cards.text: And sharing now leads somewhere: being overjoyed when His glory is revealed. Then Peter gets specific about one kind of suffering, being insulted for the name of Christ.

cards.question: Peter says a believer who is insulted for the name of Christ is blessed.
Why does Peter call the believer who is insulted for Christ's name blessed?

answers.text: The Spirit of glory rests on them
Their insulters will be punished at once
They will win the argument later

cards.text: Now Peter draws a line, because not all suffering is the same. None of them should suffer as a murderer, a thief or a wrongdoer.

cards.question: Peter adds one more to that list of ways a believer should never suffer. What is it?

cards.text: A MEDDLER, on the same list as murderer! I once stuck my mustache into an argument between the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, and I got zapped from BOTH sides.

cards.question: But if they suffer as a Christian, Peter says not to be ___, and to glorify God that they bear that name.

cards.text: Then Peter turns the page, friend. It's time, he says, for judgment to begin.

cards.question: Peter says judgment begins with the ___ of God.
If judgment begins with God's family, what does Peter ask next?

answers.text: What awaits those who disobey the gospel
How long the judgment will last
Who will stand as the judge

cards.text: Then Peter adds a quote: "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?"

cards.question: In the quote Peter adds, the ungodly and the sinner have an easier road than the righteous.

cards.text: So then. Peter's been building to this, and here it comes for everyone who suffers according to God's will.

cards.question: What does Peter say those who suffer according to God's will should do with their souls?

answers.text: Entrust them to their faithful Creator
Guard them by keeping out of sight
Hold them back until the trial passes

cards.question: Peter says those who suffer according to God's will should stop doing good until the trial is over.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke and adds nothing new from the passage. It repeats 1 Peter 4:12, which cards 1 and 2 already covered, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "Peter's answer to the heat is NOT what you'd expect" sets up card 4 and rules out its expected wrong answers ("complain" and "hide"). That points the baker to "rejoice."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to guess the next item in Peter's list (meddler, liar or drunkard). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out. It tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke about "meddler." It repeats 1 Peter 4:15, which cards 9 and 10 already covered, and adds no new moment from the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Entrust them to their faithful Creator," uses Bible-sounding wording. The wrong answers ("Guard them by keeping out of sight" and "Hold them back until the trial passes") are plain and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
